or a simpler mechanism.","did":"Interpreted the AD agent as implementing a simple heuristic (move to where the previous episode ended in reward 1, otherwise move pseudorandomly) rather than a general-purpose RL algorithm.","alternatives_named":["AD agent implements a reasonably general RL algorithm / is a mesa-optimizer"],"stated_reason":"Once the input contains an episode ending in reward 1, the model can directly infer the goal location, so no general planning or exploration-exploitation balancing is needed.","quote":"it suffices to implement the much simpler heuristic \"if your input contains an episode ending in reward 1, then move towards the position the agent was in at the end of that episode; otherwise, move around pseudorandomly.\""},{"point":"D5","problem":"How to judge whether the training and deployment tasks in the paper are genuinely different, which determines whether generalization to them demonstrates a general algorithm.","did":"Argued that tasks differing only in goal location should not count as different under a reasonable notion of task.","alternatives_named":["counting each goal location as a distinct task, as the paper does"],"stated_reason":"The training tasks are extremely similar to each other and to the deployment task, so they only count as different under a pathologically narrow notion of task.","quote":"First the training tasks used in this paper are all *extremely* similar to each other and to the deployment task; in fact, I think they only ought to count as *different* under a pathologically narrow notion of \"task.\""},{"point":"D1","problem":"Which experiments to scrutinize when assessing the paper's claims.","did":"Focused the analysis on the Dark Room family of experiments, claiming the critique generalizes to the paper's other experiments.","alternatives_named":["analyzing all experiments in the paper individually"],"stated_reason":"Concreteness; the author says the complaint applies equally to the other experiments.","quote":"For concreteness, I'll focus here on one family of experiments, Dark Room, that appeared in the paper, but my complaint applies just as well to the other experiments in the paper."},{"point":"D2","problem":"What evidence would convincingly show that AD learns a general RL algorithm rather than a narrow heuristic.","did":"Specified that in-context learning of a non-trivially different task (e.g. keys and boxes) after Dark Room training would count as strong evidence of a mesa-optimizer.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"Such a task would not be solvable by the simple 'navigate to a fixed grid position' heuristic.","quote":"If the AD agent trained in this paper were able to learn to do any non-trivially different task (e.g. an AD agent trained on Dark Room tasks were able to in-context learn a task involving collecting keys and unlocking boxes), then I would take that as strong evidence"},{"point":"D3","problem":"Whether AD outperforming expert distillation (ED) refutes the simple-heuristic interpretation.","did":"Declined to treat the ED vs AD gap as strong evidence against his interpretation, explaining it via uninformative rewards in expert data.","alternatives_named":["treating ED's failure as evidence that AD learns a real RL algorithm"],"stated_reason":"ED training data has every episode ending in reward 1, so ED cannot learn to respond differently to different rewards.","quote":"The result is that the rewards in these training data are *very uninformative* \\-\\- every episode ends with reward 1 and no episodes end with a 0, so there's no chance for the ED agents to learn to respond differently to different rewards."},{"point":"D5","problem":"How to interpret the authors' explanation that ED fails because it cannot explore while AD can.","did":"Agreed that AD explores but interpreted its exploration as mimicking an incompetent RL agent rather than sophisticated exploration.","alternatives_named":["AD performing sophisticated exploration as part of a general RL algorithm"],"stated_reason":"Under his heuristic account, AD simply imitates incompetent early-training agents when it does not know the goal.","quote":"But the sort of exploration that the AD agent does is likely \"when you don't know what to do, mimic an incompetent RL agent\" rather than some more sophisticated exploration as part of a general RL algorithm."},{"point":"D6","problem":"How strongly to state the claim about what the AD agents actually learned, given the lack of direct verification.","did":"Hedged the claim with phrases like 'strongly suspect' and conceded the agent may have learned a few additional heuristics, while still denying mesa-optimizer status.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"The sum total of such heuristics is unlikely to be sophisticated enough to count as a mesa-optimizer.","quote":"Well, probably the AD agent learned a total"},{"point":"D5","problem":"What the ED agents do at deployment given they fail to improve, with no direct data in the paper to settle it.","did":"Guessed that ED agents pick one goal position describe.","quote":"In fact, I'd guess that ED agents tend to pick some particular goal position from their training data and iteratively navigate to that goal position, never incurring reward so long
